Seduced
sē-dūst´
v. (led astray; rendering Hebrew taah, Greek planao)
From Latin seducere, to lead aside. Seduction is a leading, which means it requires a guide and a road.

Biblical Definition

To be seduced is to be led astray. Isaiah charges leaders with it: “they that lead thee cause thee to err” (Isa 9:16), and Ezekiel condemns prophets that “have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace” (Eze 13:10). John writes, “these things have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you” (1Jn 2:26), and Paul warns of “seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils” in the latter times (1Ti 4:1).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines seduce as to draw aside or entice from the path of rectitude and duty in any manner, by flattery, promises, bribes or otherwise; to tempt and lead to iniquity; to corrupt.

expand to see more

SEDUCE, v.t. To draw aside or entice from the path of rectitude and duty in any manner, by flattery, promises, bribes or otherwise; to tempt and lead to iniquity; to corrupt; to deprave.

SEDUCER, n. One who seduces; one who by temptation or arts, entices another to depart from the path of rectitude and duty.

Key Scripture

Eze 13:10 — "Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter:"

1Jn 2:26 — "These things have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you."

1Ti 4:1 — "Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils;"

Isa 9:16 — "For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed."

Modern Corruption

False comfort is mistaken for pastoral kindness, and Ezekiel's charge against the seducing prophets is one sentence: they said Peace, and there was no peace.

expand to see more

Ezekiel 13:10 identifies the mechanism of seduction as reassurance rather than temptation: because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace. The image that follows is builders daubing a flimsy wall with untempered morter — making a dangerous structure look finished. Nobody was told to sin; they were told everything was fine. That is a gentler-sounding and more effective way to destroy a congregation.

1 John 2:26-27 pairs the warning with a remedy that does not depend on expertise: these things have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you. But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you. Ordinary believers are given an internal witness sufficient to detect a lie, which is why John writes to the whole church rather than to its leaders about this danger.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew taah (H8582), to wander, cause to err; Greek planao (G4105), to lead astray; planos (G4108), a deceiver.

expand to see more

Hebrew taah (H8582) — to wander, seduce; Ezekiel 13:10, Isaiah 9:16, 2 Kings 21:9.

Greek planao (G4105) — to lead astray; 1 John 2:26, Revelation 2:20, 12:9.

Greek planos (G4108) — seducing, deceiving; 1 Timothy 4:1, seducing spirits.

Usage

"“Saying, Peace; and there was no peace” — seduction by reassurance."

"“Daubed it with untempered morter” — a flimsy wall made to look finished."

"“The anointing which ye have received… abideth in you” — the remedy given to all."
